messages.title: Can the Old Worker Still Commit?
messages.subtitle: Worker B has taken over Job J, but Worker A is still running. Which component decides whether A can make its result authoritative?
messages.property: Once generation 8 becomes current, generation 7 must not make Job J's protected result authoritative.
messages.takeaway: We did not stop the stale worker. We prevented stale authority from changing protected state.
messages.challenge.title: Can A7 commit?
messages.challenge.intro: Worker A acquired generation 7. Worker B later acquired generation 8 but has not committed. Job J is still RUNNING. StoreResult accepts any result while the job is RUNNING; it does not compare generations.
messages.challenge.question: Under this Store contract, can A7 make its result authoritative?
messages.option.yes: Yes. A7 can commit under the weak contract.
messages.option.no: No. The expired lease automatically blocks A7.
messages.option.needMore: We need to inspect the Store's mutation contract.
messages.challenge.feedback: The weak Store sees RUNNING and accepts A7. B8 has not committed, so a terminal-state guard cannot save this execution. The repair must atomically compare the presented generation with the Store's current generation.
messages.deepDive.title: What does the generation gate protect?
messages.deepDive.section1.title: A local lease check can go stale
messages.deepDive.section1.body: A checks lease.Valid() and sees true. A pauses. B acquires generation 8. A resumes and calls StoreResult. Only a check at the protected mutation can reject the stale generation at that moment.
messages.deepDive.section2.title: A terminal-state guard proves something else
messages.deepDive.section2.body: If B had committed first, DONE might reject A. That does not isolate stale authority. In the counterexample, B has not committed and the job is still RUNNING when A resumes.
messages.deepDive.section3.title: A nonparticipating provider remains exposed
messages.deepDive.section3.body: The Job Store may reject A7 while an email provider still accepts A's SendEmail call. A generation number protects only resources that participate in its enforcement protocol.
messages.deepDive.section4.title: Transfer: document publishing
messages.deepDive.section4.body: Editor A holds revision generation 12. Editor B later acquires 13. If the publication store requires presented_generation == current_generation, A12 cannot publish after 13 becomes current, while B13 can.
messages.visual.title: Authority timeline
messages.visual.aPaused: A pauses; losing the lease does not erase A
messages.visual.bCurrent: B takes over; generation 8 is current
messages.visual.aAccepted: Weak Store accepts A7 while RUNNING
messages.visual.external: The external email provider has no generation gate
messages.rail.evidenceEarly: A acquired generation 7 and may continue executing.
messages.rail.contractEarly: Authority can move to a later generation.
messages.rail.propertyHidden: Which result may become authoritative is not established yet.
messages.rail.evidenceTakeover: B acquired generation 8. A may resume. B has not committed, and Job J is RUNNING.
messages.rail.contractWeak: The weak Store checks RUNNING but does not compare generations.
messages.rail.property: After generation 8 becomes current, generation 7 must not commit the protected result.
messages.rail.contractStrong: The Store atomically requires RUNNING and presented_generation == current_generation.
messages.rail.scope: An external provider without the generation protocol can still accept A's side effect.
messages.anchor.local-authority-check: Local check that can go stale
messages.recap.1: Evidence: A acquired 7; B later acquired 8; A can still run.
messages.recap.2: Weak execution: A7 can call StoreResult while Job J is still RUNNING.
messages.recap.3: Property: A7 must not make the result authoritative after 8 becomes current.
messages.recap.4: Enforcement: the Job Store atomically compares the presented and current generations.
messages.recap.5: Repair: A7 is rejected; B8 can commit normally.
messages.recap.6: Remaining surface: a resource that does not enforce generation may still accept A's side effects.
messages.step.review.title: The ordinary worker
messages.step.review.lead: The worker processes Job J and calls StoreResult(jobID, result). The call looks reasonable, but it carries no proof of the authority the worker acquired.
messages.step.acquire-a.title: A starts with generation 7
messages.step.acquire-a.lead: Worker A acquires Job J at generation 7 and starts processing. A held authority at that point; it is not guaranteed to hold it forever.
messages.step.pause-a.title: A pauses, but still exists
messages.step.pause-a.lead: A stops heartbeating and pauses. Losing the lease does not guarantee the process stops; A may later resume with its old result.
messages.step.takeover-b.title: B receives generation 8
messages.step.takeover-b.lead: Worker B takes over. The Job Store records current_generation = 8, superseding A's generation 7.
messages.step.b-uncommitted.title: Keep the job RUNNING
messages.step.b-uncommitted.lead: B has started but has not committed. Job J is still RUNNING when A resumes. This isolates stale authority from terminal-state protection.
messages.step.decision.title: Can A still commit?
messages.step.decision.lead: A presents its result after B's takeover. Decide from the Store contract, not from an intuition that only one worker should be active.
messages.step.weak-contract.title: Read the weak Store contract
messages.step.weak-contract.lead: StoreResult(jobID, result) checks that Job J exists and state == RUNNING. It does not compare A's acquired generation with current_generation.
messages.step.counterexample.title: A stale result becomes authoritative
messages.step.counterexample.lead: A7 resumes and calls StoreResult. Because Job J is RUNNING, the weak Store accepts A's result even though current_generation is 8. The property is violated.
messages.step.property.title: Name the property
messages.step.property.lead: Once generation 8 is current, generation 7 must not make Job J's protected result authoritative. The property does not require A to stop executing.
messages.step.strong-contract.title: Move the check to the mutation
messages.step.strong-contract.lead: StoreResult now carries acquiredGeneration. The Job Store atomically requires state == RUNNING and acquired_generation == current_generation.
messages.step.reject-a.title: A7 is rejected
messages.step.reject-a.lead: A presents 7 while the Store holds 8. The protected mutation is rejected, even if A is still running.
messages.step.accept-b.title: B8 is accepted
messages.step.accept-b.lead: B presents 8 while the Store holds 8 and Job J is RUNNING. The generation gate accepts B's result; the repair does not reject every write.
messages.step.scope-challenge.title: Test the next boundary
messages.step.scope-challenge.lead: If an email provider does not check generations, the Job Store's gate cannot prevent A's external side effect. Each protected resource must participate in the protocol.
messages.step.remaining.title: State the remaining surface
messages.step.remaining.lead: The repair does not stop stale workers, protect arbitrary external APIs, prove B will finish, or make every side effect generation-aware. It protects the Job Store mutation.
messages.step.recap.title: Six Questions recap
messages.step.recap.lead: The weak contract admitted A7 while RUNNING. The generation-gated Store rejects A7 and accepts B8. The enforcement boundary, not the worker lifecycle, decides the result.
